about.title: Aliso Viejo Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Aliso Viejo's mix of corporate campuses, retail centers, and construction near growing developments means workplace injuries happen in offices, warehouses, and job sites throughout the city. In most cases, California law routes injured workers through the workers' compensation system, which pays medical care and partial wage replacement regardless of fault, but limits your recovery against your employer. What many injured workers don't realize is that a third party — a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or delivery driver — may share responsibility for the accident, opening the door to a separate injury claim outside the workers' comp system. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims directly; we simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney in our network who can review the facts of your workplace incident and explain whether pursuing a third-party claim alongside your workers' comp benefits makes sense for your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Aliso Viejo Workers Ask LawProactive First

items.title: We Understand the Exclusive Remedy Rule
items.desc: California generally requires injured workers to go through workers' compensation rather than suing their employer directly. An attorney can help you understand how this applies and whether it limits your options.

items.title: We Help You Spot Third-Party Liability
items.desc: If a subcontractor, equipment maker, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim beyond workers' comp. The attorneys in our network can evaluate whether a third party bears responsibility.

items.title: We Know the Deadlines That Matter
items.desc: Workplace injuries generally must be reported to your employer within 30 days, and any third-party injury claim is subject to California's two-year statute of limitations. Missing either window can close off options, so timing matters.

items.question: I was hurt at my job in Aliso Viejo — do I have to use workers' comp?
items.answer: In most cases, yes, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer even if the injury wasn't your fault. However, if someone other than your employer contributed to the accident, such as a contractor or equipment manufacturer, you may be able to bring a separate claim. An independent attorney can review the details and explain your options.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work near Aliso Creek Road or Alicia Parkway?
items.answer: If you were injured in a vehicle collision while performing work duties on corridors like Aliso Creek Road or Alicia Parkway, you may have both a workers' comp claim and a potential third-party claim against another driver. These situations often involve overlapping deadlines and rules, so getting an attorney's input early can help clarify your path forward.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury or file a claim in Aliso Viejo?
items.answer: California generally requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. If a third party is involved and you're pursuing a separate injury claim, that claim typically must be filed within two years of the incident. Because these timelines differ and interact, it's worth discussing your specific situation with an attorney sooner rather than later.
